diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber router has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the >4 hour danger threshold. The router is therefore unreachable or its management/heartbeat path is down, while the EPON link, OLT, authentication, VLAN, and subscriber session remain healthy.
evidence: The alarm is for a stale router heartbeat of 7.4 hours; heartbeat age above 4 hours is classified as danger.
The ONU is online and responds successfully, with RX -20.61 dBm and TX +2.40 dBm in the normal ranges.
The 168-hour optical telemetry is stable: RX remains around -20.6 dBm, TX remains around +2.35 dBm, distance is constant at 152, and bias current is stable near 11.2 mA.
All visible peers on EPON0/2 are online, so there is no evidence of an ONU, splitter, PON-port, or shared fibre fault.
The OLT answers ping and SNMP, all eight PONs are healthy, and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are normal; the OLT is not the cause.
The subscriber has one session in the last 24 hours with a duration near the network mean, so there is no session flapping.
RADIUS records match CRM and the expected VLAN 1062 is present, ruling out authentication and provisioning faults.
The only abnormal current-state signal is the router heartbeat age, so the fault is scoped to the router.

remediation.action: Verify router reachability and management-plane connectivity, including ping, SSH/API, power, uplink, and heartbeat-agent status. Restore or restart the router/heartbeat service as appropriate, then confirm a fresh check-in. Do not dispatch fibre or OLT work unless the router and uplink checks identify a physical fault.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
